newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - June 19.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:

* The Senate Finance Committee passed a package of health legislation that would revamp Medicare, increase charges levied on affluent elderly recipients, provide new money for health coverage of uninsured children and restore welfare benefits for more than 500,000 legal immigrants.
* Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan resigned after nearly a year in power amidst pressure from the military.
* Cambodian Khmer Rouge leader Pol Pot has surrendered to his former comrades-turned-enemies, according to an unconfirmed radio report.

* A tea house waiter, a fishmonger, a middle-class teacher and a tycoon from one of Hong Kong's oldest Chinese merchant families tell their stories as Hong Kong prepares to pass from British to Chinese sovereignty.
* Hormone replacement after menopause can greatly reduce a woman's risk of death as long as the therapy is continued, a study has found.
* Walt Disney Co is under fire from Southern Baptists, who have launched a boycott over concerns about the company's policies toward gays and some of the movies Disney has churned out recently.
* Lehman Brothers is selling One Times Square for about $110 million, ringing up a hefty profit from the $27.5 million it doled out for the property two years ago, sources said.
* "Cats," the broadway show, has more than nine lives. In fact, it's had 6,138 live performances -- the longest-running show in Broadway history.
* New York Chief Judge Judith Kaye said the state's family court system should be open routinely to the public.
